previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted with worsening shortness of breath, leg swelling, and elevated creatinine. She had recently been treated for recurrent C. diff and presented with acute on chronic diastolic heart failure and acute kidney injury likely due to poor forward flow. She was managed with IV and then oral furosemide, fluid restriction, and close monitoring. Her heart failure symptoms improved, and kidney function stabilized. The C. diff treatment was completed during admission with no ongoing diarrhea. She remained medically stable for several weeks, but discharge was delayed due to logistical issues. She was discharged home with services, on her baseline diuretic, with follow-up planned for cardiology, nephrology, and primary care.

Brief Hospital Course:
___ yo female with complicated past medical history of chronic 
kidney disease, coronary ___ disease status post three vessel 
coronary artery bypass surgery, hypertension, hyperlipidemia, 
diastolic heart failure, insulin dependent diabetes type II 
requiring multiple hospitalizations now presents with nausea, 
shortness of breath, failure to thrive at home with a chest 
x-ray showing pulmonary congestion concerning for an acute 
diastolic heart failure exacerbation. 

## Diastolic heart failure exacerbation: Patient was admitted 
for shortness of breath with chest x-ray showing pulmonary edema 
consistent with ___ exacerbation and an exam notable for 
elevated jugular venous pressure and 1+ edema bilaterally to 
knees. Labs were notable for an elevated BNP from baseline, and 
a mild transaminitis suggesting hepatic congestion. 
(Transaminitis resolved with diuresis. Abdominal ultrasound did 
not show any cholelithiasis). The etiology for her CHF 
decompensation is unclear but may be related to medication 
noncompliance in the setting of nausea. On admission, patient 
was diuresed with IV lasix with goal of 1 to 2 liters negative 
daily, and monitored with daily weights, strict in and outs, and 
2L fluid restriction. When patient was transitioned back to PO 
lasix on her home dose however patient did not diurese well, so 
toresemide was started for suspected gut edema. Patient 
responded well to PO toresmide and will continue it on 
discharge.

## Pansensitive klebsiella urinary tract infection: Patient 
reported pain with urination and urine culture showed 
pansensitive klebsiella (although there was a question of fecal 
contamination). Patient was treated with ceftriaxone and 
ciprofloxacin for a total of four days. However patient 
continued to endorse dysuria after treatment, so repeat urine 
analysis and urine culture was sent, which were negative. Mrs. 
___ was started on Estrace for suspected vaginal dryness/ 
atrophic vaginitis as contributing to her dysuria. Patient 
should follow-up with an urologist for further evaluation if the 
Estrace does not improve symptoms, and an appointment has been 
scheduled. 

## Rule out myocardial infarction: On admission patient reported 
increased chest pressure and nausea which may be concerning for 
new myocardial infarction. However patient's EKG was unchanged 
from baseline, and she had two negative troponins (at baseline). 


## Diarrhea: Patient reported two episodes of diarrhea at home 
and had only one episode while in the hospital. No other work-up 
was initiated given lack of other associated symptoms, no travel 
history, dietary changes, or electrolyte abnormalities. 

## Deconditioning: Patient worked with physical therapy to 
increase her strength and her balance. Patient improved and was 
able to walk 6 stairs on discharge. Thus in case of an 
emergency, she will be able to safely evacuate her home. Patient 
will follow-up with home ___. She should do stairs on her home, 
no one should be allowed to 'haul' her up the stairs into her 
apartment, as that puts her at risk to herself and to the others 
helping her. 

## Anemia of chronic disease: Patient has normocytic anemia with 
normal Fe and high ferritin. Patient was recommended to 
follow-up with an nephrologist as an outpatient to consider 
starting epogen.

## Hypertension: Patient was hypertensive with blood 
pressure>130/80s, so we uptitrated her hydralazine to 100 mg 
QH8. She was continued on her other anti-hypertensives per her 
home regimen. 

## Chronic kidney disease: Patient's creatinine was in 2.1 - 2.7 
range, which is at her baseline. Patient should follow up with 
primary care doctor in one week to check her electrolytes that 
she is on PO toresemide. We also renally dosed her medications.

## Coronary artery disease: Stable. Patient's metoprolol was 
decreased to 12.5 BID as patient was mildly bradycardic to ___. 
She is not on an ACEi because of a history of hyperkalemia. 

## Cerebral vascular accident: Stable. Patient was continued on 
plavix. She has an aspirin allergy. 

## Insulin dependent diabetes type II: Stable. Patient was on 
insulin sliding scale with gabapentin for neuropathy.

Discharge Instructions:
You were admitted for shortness of breath because you had fluid 
in your lungs. We gave you IV lasix which helped get the fluid 
out of your lungs. We tried giving you PO lasix, but you were 
not responding well to that medicine, so we switched you to 
torsemide, which is another water pill.

You also were found to have a urinary tract infection while in 
the hospital. We treated you with antibiotics, and on repeat 
testing, you no longer had the infection. However because you 
are continuing to experience burning on urination, you should 
follow-up with an urologist as an outpatient. We also prescribed 
Estrace a vaginal cream for vaginal dryness as they may be 
contributing to your pain on urination.

Your heart rate was low during this admission so we decreased 
your dose of metoprolol to 12.5 mg two times a day by mouth.  
Your blood pressures were high, so we changed your hydralazine 
from 80 to 100 three times a day.

On this admission we also found that you were deconditioned and 
had difficulty walking around. You improved with the help of 
physical therapy. It is important to continue to work with ___ 
when you go home because you will need to be able to get out of 
the house in emergency situations. It is not recommended that 
someone haul you up the stairs of your house to get in after 
dischage, that is unsafe for both you and the person helping 
you. 

Lastly we found that your blood count was low so we gave you a 
transfusion. Your anemia is most likely related to your chronic 
kidney disease. You should see a nephrologists as an outpatient 
to discuss starting epogen.

In summary we made the following changes to your medications:
1) We stopped your lasix and switched you to TORSEMIDE 20 by 
mouth daily
2) We decreased your METOPROLOL to 12.5 mg two times a day
3) We increased your HYDRALAZINE to 100 mg three times a day
4) We added vaginal cream ESTRACE vaginal cream. Please apply 
once a night for 2 weeks for vaginal dryness as this may be 
contributing to your pain on urination.

When you leave the hospital, you should:
1) Continue to work with ___ so that you can get out of your 
house in the case of an emergency. 
2) Follow-up with in ___ with Dr. ___ (Dr. ___ 
to monitor your new medications, discuss next steps in making 
your daughter ___ your power of attorney. Please also have 
your electrolytes re-checked at this appointment.
3) Weigh yourself every morning, and call MD if weight goes up 
more than 3 lbs.
4) Follow up with your new kidney doctor to discuss starting 
epogen because you are anemic. 
5) Attempt the vaginal cream for your burning on urination. If 
this does not improve, please see an urologist for your urinary 
pain
.
